title: My First Video (Remake)
transcript: Bishop to b6 is a brilliant sacrifice that cannot be accepted because otherwise white would be able to push the pawn towards promotion. And since this is a dark square bishop, it would never be able to defend a light square. So, white would win. And if the bishop captured, now after pawn takes, white would be threatening again the promotion and this would be [music] winning. But black is not that naive and he knows that he doesn't have to capture the white bishop. Instead, he can simply play bishop to f2, removing the black bishop from the pressure of the king. And of course, if white was to capture here, now he would have no leverage to create a passed pawn. So, this would actually just be a draw. But white has a brilliant plan to make progress and he simply plays king to h2, re-sacrificing the bishop. Because of course, it still cannot be taken. Black doesn't really want to move away from the defense of his own pawn. And if he moves along this diagonal, of course, white would simply be able to capture. So, he has to move the king and still maintain the standoff. But now white plays king to g2, sacrificing that bishop for a third time in a row and now creating a threat of capturing the black bishop. So, black has to evade again. And now we start to see the pattern. This is an incredible multiple sacrifice king ladder where every move sacrifices the bishop again and again to make progress with the king. And eventually we reach this point where the black bishop has nowhere else to go. But black has one last surprising resource and he's the one to throw a brilliancy at white with bishop to g1. Because if white was to take the bishop, now the black king is close enough to capture this pawn and there is no way to defend the a6 pawn, which means that this would end in a textbook bishop and pawn ending that is actually drawn since the dark square bishop can never support the promotion square. So, is this it? Is this position simply a draw? Well, not exactly because all that white has to do is follow his heart and sacrifice the bishop one last time. And this time there is no choice. If you take the bishop, we already know that this is winning for white. And if black tries to sacrifice again, white can now capture the bishop because after king takes, white has king to b7, defending his promoting pawn. And the black king has no way to access the corner, which means that white is going to be able to promote and finally win this incredible ending.
